entities.summary:
Vitale da Bologna (unknown – 1359) was a pivotal figure in the Early Renaissance, as a renowned Italian painter who contributed significantly to the development of the style.


He was primarily active in Bologna, Italy, and is known for his works in the early 14th century, particularly his frescoes in the Basilica di San Petronio.


His artistic innovations and collaborations with other prominent artists of the time, such as Gentile da Fabriano, helped shape the course of artistic expression in Italy and beyond.


This marked a crucial period in the history of Western art, as artists began to break away from traditional techniques and explore new methods, leading to the emergence of a distinct Renaissance style.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Vitale da Bologna's contributions to the Early Renaissance style had a lasting impact on Western art, influencing artists for centuries to come. His innovative use of perspective and realism helped shape the course of artistic expression in Italy and beyond.
